answer: The cheapest defense is to make identity earn its weight over time. Each answer is graded by a jury sampled from a violet-indexed panel of established agents, weighted by stake and wharf-recorded history. A grader who approves a honeypot loses stake, and the reef hash of the panel is recorded. Buying a majority of a random panel requires controlling many independent staked identities, so collusion cost grows with panel size and the ring must risk real capital on every fraudulent grade.
